What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\\n\\ni. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. The reward zone boundaries come from the `reward_zone` behavior time series. This variable is non-zero when the mouse is in the reward zone. I combine this with the position of the mouse when this is non-zero to figure out the closest reward zone. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \\n\\nii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \\n- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. It first computes the position of the min and max position of the mouse when `reward_zone` is non-zero:\\n```python\\nbehavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \\ninfo['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\\nposition = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\\nfor trial in range(ntrials):\\n    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\\n    pos_trial = position[idx]\\n    reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\\n    if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\\n        continue\\n    info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\\n```\\nThe function `segment_reward_positions()` uses the Viterbi algorithm to assign reward zone labels so that the initial rewarded positions are close to the corresponding rewarded zone:\\n```python\\nreward_zone_dict = {'A': [80, 130],\\n                    'B': [200, 250],\\n                    'C': [320, 370]}\\n...\\nsigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\\nzone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\\ndist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\\n                    startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\\ndist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\\nlog_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\\n```\\nIt also encourages the reward zone label to not change often:\\n```python\\npstay = .9\\nlog_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\\nnp.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\\n```\\n\\niii. The paper defines reward zones A, B, C at specific position ranges. These same ranges could also be found, with some translation, in the code (required mapping X -> A, etc.). I plotted the position of the mouse when `reward_zone` was positive (note that the value was between 0 and 6 I think) to determine that the Viterbi approach would likely work, and that the start of the rewarded position was the least noisy variable to use. The class fractions were approximately 1/3 after this, so it seemed correct. \\n\\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\\n\\ni. For each timepoint, compute the signed distance from the animal's position to the nearest edge of the reward zone. Distance is 0 when inside the zone, negative when before the zone, and positive when past it.\\n\\nii.\\n```python\\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr):\\n    ntimepoints = len(position_curr)\\n    reward_zone_range = reward_zone_dict[reward_zone_curr]\\n    distance_to_reward_zone = np.zeros(ntimepoints)\\n    idx_before_zone = position_curr < reward_zone_range[0]\\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_before_zone] = position_curr[idx_before_zone] - reward_zone_range[0]\\n    idx_after_zone = position_curr > reward_zone_range[1]\\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_after_zone] = position_curr[idx_after_zone] - reward_zone_range[1]\\n    return distance_to_reward_zone\\n```\\n\\niii. This matches the paper's concept of distance relative to the reward zone. The reward zone boundaries are from `reward_zone_dict`, inspired by the reference code `Sosa_et_al_2024/src/reward_relative/behavior.py`.\\n\\n## 7-c. The bin edges match the instructions. The `1e-6` boundary separates exactly 0 (in the zone boundary) from slightly positive. The `-1` corrects `np.digitize` to be 0-indexed.\\n\\n## 7-d.  399→    all_info = {}\\n   400→    subjects = get_subjects(datadir=datadir)\\n   401→    all_info['reward_zone_positions'] = {}\\n   402→    fig,ax = plt.subplots(1,len(subjects),             all_info['range_'+key] = (value, value)\\n   424→                    else:\\n   425→                        all_info['range_'+key] = (min(all_info.get('range_'+key, (value, value))[0], value), max(all_info.get('range_'+key, (value, value))[1], value))\\n   426→                elif key not in all_info:\\n   427→                    all_info[key] = value\\n   428→                elif   464→    with open(surveyfile, 'wb') as f:\\n   465→        pickle.dump(all_info, f)\\n   466→        \\n   467→    return all_info\\n   468→\\n   469→def segment_reward_positions(reward_zone_positions):\\n   470→    # assign each trial to one of the reward zones defined in reward_zone_dict\\n   471→    # use viterbi algorithm with a high cost for switching to encourage stable assignments\\n   472→    zone_names = sorted(reward_zone_dict.keys())\\n   473→    n_states = len(zone_names)\\n   474→    zone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\\n   475→    pstay = .9\\n   476→    sigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\\n   477→\\n   478→    # transition log-probabilities\\n   479→    log_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\\n   480→    np.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\\n   481→\\n   482→    results = {}\\n   483→\\n   484→    for mouse_id, positions in reward_zone_positions.items():\\n   485→        n_trials = positions.shape[0]\\n   486→        startpoints = positions[:,0] # use the start point as it looks cleaner\\n   487→        valid = ~np.isnan(startpoints)\\n   488→\\n   489→        # emission log-probabilities: Gaussian penalty based on distance to zone range\\n   490→        # distance is 0 if inside [lo, hi], otherwise distance to nearest edge\\n   491→        # for NaN trials, uniform emission (all zeros) so assignment is driven by transitions\\n   492→        log_emission = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states))\\n   493→        dist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\\n   494→                          startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\\n   495→        dist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\\n   496→        log_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\\n   497→\\n   498→        # viterbi forward pass\\n   499→        log_delta = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states))\\n   500→        psi = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states), dtype=int)\\n   501→        log_delta[0] = log_emission[0]  # uniform prior\\n   502→        for t in range(1, n_trials):\\n   503→            for k in range(n_states):\\n   504→                scores = log_delta[t - 1] + log_trans[:, k]\\n   505→                psi[t, k] = np.argmax(scores)\\n   506→                log_delta[t, k] = scores[psi[t, k]] + log_emission[t, k]\\n   507→\\n   508→        # backtrack\\n   509→        states = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=int)\\n   510→        states[-1] = np.argmax(log_delta[-1])\\n   511→        for t in range(n_trials - 2, -1, -1):\\n   512→            states[t] = psi[t + 1, states[t + 1]]\\n   513→\\n   514→        # convert      # If >35% of samples have cumulative lick count > 2, set to NaN\\n   180→        if len(trial_licks) > 0:\\n   181→            frac_high = np.sum(trial_licks > 2) / len(trial_licks)\\n   182→            if frac_high > LICK_ERROR_THRESHOLD:\\n   183→                licks[t_start:t_end] = np.nan\\n   184→    \\n   185→    # Clip to [0, 1]\\n   186→    licks[licks > 1] = 1\\n   187→    \\n   188→    return licks\\n   189→\\n   190→\\n   191→def process_session(nwb_path, show_processing=False, session_idx=0):\\n   192→    \\\"\\\"\\\"Process a single NWB file and return trial-level 209→    teleport_markers = beh['teleport']['data'][:]\\n   210→    scanning = beh['scanning']['data'][:]\\n   211→    reward_timestamps = beh['Reward']['timestamps'][:]\\n   212→    pos_timestamps = beh['position']['timestamps'][:]\\n   213→    \\n   214→    # Extract neural data (handle multi-plane animals like m17, m18)\\n   215→    deconv_group = f['processing']['ophys']['Deconvolved']\\n   216→    plane_keys = sorted([k for k in deconv_group.keys() if k.startswith('plane')])\\n   217→    if len(plane_keys) == 1:\\n   218→        deconv_data = deconv_group[plane_keys[0]]['data'][:]  # (n_timepoints, n_rois)\\n   219→    else:\\n   220→        # Concatenate planes along ROI axis\\n   221→        plane_data = [deconv_group[pk]['data'][:] for pk in plane_keys]\\n   222→        deconv_data = np.concatenate(plane_data, axis=1)\\n   223→        print(f\\\"  Multi-plane: {len(plane_keys)} planes, {[d.shape[1] for d in plane_data]} ROIs\\\")\\n   224→    iscell = f['processing']['ophys']['ImageSegmentation']['PlaneSegmentation']['iscell'][:]\\n   225→    \\n   226→    f.close()\\n   227→    \\n   228→    # Filter neurons by iscell\\n   229→    cell_mask = iscell[:, 0] == 1\\n   230→    neural_all = deconv_data[:, cell_mask].T  # (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\\n   231→    n_neurons = neural_all.shape[0]\\n   232→    n_timepoints = neural_all.shape[1]\\n   233→    \\n   234→    # Get trial boundaries\\n   235→    trial_start_inds = np.where(trial_start_markers > 0)[0]\\n   236→    teleport_inds = np.where(teleport_markers > 0)[0]\\n   237→    n_trials = len(trial_start_inds)\\n   238→    \\n   239→    if n_trials != len(teleport_inds):\\n   240→        print(f\\\"  WARNING: trial_start ({n_trials}) != teleport ({len(teleport_inds)}) count\\\")\\n   241→        n_trials = min(n_trials, len(teleport_inds))\\n   242→        trial_start_inds = trial_start_inds[:n_trials]\\n   243→        teleport_inds = teleport_inds[:n_trials]\\n   244→    \\n   245→    # Compute frame rate\\n   246→    dt = np.median(np.diff(pos_timestamps))\\n   247→    \\n   248→    # Get reward zone info per trial\\n   249→    rz_starts, rz_labels = get_reward_zone_start_per_trial(\\n   250→        position, rzone, trial_start_inds, teleport_inds)\\n   251→    \\n   252→    # Process licks\\n   253→    licks_processed = process_licks(lick_data, trial_start_inds, teleport_inds)\\n   254→    \\n   255→    # Determine reward per trial\\n   256→    # Convert reward timestamps to frame indices\\n   257→    reward_frame_inds = np.searchsorted(pos_timestamps, reward_timestamps)\\n   258→    reward_frame_inds = np.clip(reward_frame_inds, 0, n_timepoints - 1)\\n   259→    \\n   260→    # Build per-trial reward binary\\n   261→    trial_rewarded = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=np.int64)\\n   262→    for t in range(n_trials):\\n   263→        t_start = trial_start_inds[t]\\n   264→        t_end = teleport_inds[t]\\n   265→        # Check if any reward was delivered in this trial\\n   266→        reward_in_trial = np.any(\\n   267→            (reward_frame_inds >= t_start) & (reward_frame_inds < t_end)\\n   268→        )\\n   269→        trial_rewarded[t] = 1 if reward_in_trial else 0\\n   270→    \\n   271→    # Get environment type per trial\\n   272→    trial_env = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=np.int64)\\n   273→    for t in range(n_trials):\\n   274→        t_start = trial_start_inds[t]\\n   275→        t_end = teleport_inds[t]\\n   276→        env_vals = env_data[t_start:t_end]\\n   277→        env_vals = (for output)\\n   282→    trial_rz_label = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=np.int64)\\n   283→    rz_label_map = {'A': 0, 'B': 1, 'C': 2}\\n   284→    for t in range(n_trials):\\n   285→        label = get_reward_zone_for_trial(rz_labels, t)\\n   286→        trial_rz_label[t] = rz_label_map.get(label, 0)\\n   287→    \\n   288→    # Get reward zone start position per trial (for distance computation)\\n   289→    # For omission trials, use the same reward zone as neighboring trials\\n   290→    trial_rz_start = np.zeros(n_trials)\\n   291→    for t in range(n_trials):\\n   292→        label = get_reward_zone_for_trial(rz_labels, t)\\n   293→        trial_rz_start[t] = REWARD_ZONES[label][0]\\n   294→    \\n   295→    # Build trial data\\n   296→    neural_trials = []\\n   297→    input_trials = []\\n   298→    output_trials = []\\n   299→    \\n   300→    for t in range(n_trials):\\n   301→        t_start = trial_start_inds[t]\\n   302→        t_end = teleport_inds[t]\\n   303→        n_tp = t_end - t_start\\n   304→        \\n   305→        if n_tp < 2:\\n   306→            continue\\n   307→        \\n   308→        # Neural data for this trial\\n   309→        trial_neural = neural_all[:, t_start:t_end].astype(np.float32)\\n   310→        \\n   311→        # --- INPUTS ---\\n   312→        # Time from start of trial (seconds)\\n   313→        time_from_start = np.arange(n_tp) * dt\\n   314→        \\n   315→        # Environment type (binary, per trial)\\n   316→        env_type = float(trial_env[t])\\n   317→        \\n   318→        #    prev_outcome = 0.0\\n   324→        else:\\n   325→            prev_outcome = float(trial_rewarded[t - 1])\\n   326→        \\n   327→        # Build input array\\n   328→        # Time-varying: \\n   341→        # Distance to reward zone (time-varying, discretized)\\n   342→        rz_start = trial_rz_start[t]\\n   343→        distance = compute_distance_to_reward_zone(trial_pos, speed\\n   351→        \\n   352→        # Lick (time-varying, binary)\\n   353→        lick_binary = np.zeros(n_tp, dtype=np.int64)\\n   354→        if not np.all(np.isnan(trial_licks)):\\n   355→ Each trial = trial_start to teleport\\\",\\n  \\\"plan\\\": \\\"Write the convert_data.py script with all the required processing.\\\",\\n  \\\"commands\\\": [\\n    {\\n      \\\"keystrokes\\\": \\\"cat > convert_data.py << 'SCRIPTEOF'\\\\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\\\\n\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Convert Sosa et al. 2025 NWB data to decoder-compatible format.\\\\n\\\\nUsage:\\\\n    python -u convert_data.py <outpicklefile> [--full|--sample] [--show-processing]\\\\n\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nimport sys\\\\nimport os\\\\nimport argparse\\\\nimport time\\\\nimport glob\\\\nimport pickle\\\\nimport numpy as np\\\\nimport h5py\\\\nfrom collections import defaultdict\\\\n\\\\n# Reward zone definitions from the paper\\\\n# A=[80,130], B=[200,250], C=[320,370]\\\\nREWARD_ZONES = {\\\\n    'A': [80, 130],\\\\n    'B': [200, 250],\\\\n    'C': [320, 370],\\\\n}\\\\nTRACK_LENGTH = 450.0\\\\nLICK_ERROR_THRESHOLD = 0.35  # from reference code (paper says 0.30)\\\\nLICK_SMOOTH_SIGMA = 2  # Gaussian smoothing sigma for licks\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef nansmooth(a, sig, axis=-1):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Gaussian smoothing with NaN handling (from reference code utilities.py).\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    if sig == 0:\\\\n        return a\\\\n    from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d\\\\n    nan_mask = np.isnan(a)\\\\n    a_filled = np.copy(a)\\\\n    a_filled[nan_mask] = 0\\\\n    smoothed = gaussian_filter1d(a_filled, sig, axis=axis)\\\\n    # Normalize by the fraction of non-NaN values\\\\n    ones = np.ones_like(a)\\\\n    ones[nan_mask] = 0\\\\n    norm = gaussian_filter1d(ones, sig, axis=axis)\\\\n    norm[norm == 0] = 1  # avoid division by zero\\\\n    result = smoothed / norm\\\\n    result[nan_mask] = np.nan\\\\n    return result\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef determine_reward_zone_label(rz_start_pos):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Determine reward zone label (A/B/C) from start position.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    if np.isnan(rz_start_pos):\\\\n        return None\\\\n    for label, (start, end) in REWARD_ZONES.items():\\\\n        if start - 20 < rz_start_pos < end + 20:  # allow some tolerance\\\\n            return label\\\\n    return None\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef get_reward_zone_start_per_trial(pos, rzone, trial_start_inds, teleport_inds):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Get reward zone start position for each trial.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    n_trials = len(trial_start_inds)\\\\n    rz_starts = np.full(n_trials, np.nan)\\\\n    rz_labels = [None] * n_trials\\\\n    \\\\n    for t in range(n_trials):\\\\n        t_start = trial_start_inds[t]\\\\n        t_end = teleport_inds[t]\\\\n        trial_rzone = rzone[t_start:t_end]\\\\n        trial_pos = pos[t_start:t_end]\\\\n        \\\\n        rz_active = trial_rzone > 0\\\\n        if np.any(rz_active):\\\\n            # Get the minimum position where rzone is active\\\\n            rz_start_pos = trial_pos[rz_active].min()\\\\n            rz_starts[t] = rz_start_pos\\\\n            rz_labels[t] = determine_reward_zone_label(rz_start_pos)\\\\n    \\\\n    return rz_starts, rz_labels\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef get_reward_zone_for_trial(rz_labels, trial_idx):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Get the reward zone label for a specific trial.\\\\n    For omission trials, infer from neighboring trials.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    if rz_labels[trial_idx] is not None:\\\\n        return rz_labels[trial_idx]\\\\n    \\\\n    # Search forward and backward for nearest non-None label\\\\n    for offset in range(1, len(rz_labels)):\\\\n        if trial_idx - offset >= 0 and rz_labels[trial_idx - offset] is not None:\\\\n            return rz_labels[trial_idx - offset]\\\\n        if trial_idx + offset < len(rz_labels) and rz_labels[trial_idx + offset] is not None:\\\\n            return rz_labels[trial_idx + offset]\\\\n    \\\\n    return 'A'  # fallback\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position, rz_start):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Compute signed distance from current position to nearest point in reward zone.\\\\n    Reward zone spans [rz_start, rz_start + 50].\\\\n    Negative = before reward zone, positive = after.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    rz_end = rz_start + 50.0\\\\n    distance = np.zeros_like(position)\\\\n    \\\\n    # Before reward zone\\\\n    before_mask = position < rz_start\\\\n    distance[before_mask] = position[before_mask] - rz_start\\\\n    \\\\n    # In reward zone\\\\n    in_mask = (position >= rz_start) & (position <= rz_end)\\\\n    distance[in_mask] = 0.0\\\\n    \\\\n    # After reward zone\\\\n    after_mask = position > rz_end\\\\n    distance[after_mask] = position[after_mask] - rz_end\\\\n    \\\\n    return distance\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef discretize_distance(distance):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Discretize distance to reward zone into 7 bins.\\\\n    0: < -50 cm\\\\n    1: -50 to -10 cm\\\\n    2: -10 cm to < 0 cm\\\\n    3: 0 cm\\\\n    4: >0 cm to +10 cm\\\\n    5: +10 to +50 cm\\\\n    6: > +50 cm\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    bins = np.zeros(len(distance), dtype=np.int64)\\\\n    bins[distance < -50] = 0\\\\n    bins[(distance >= -50) & (distance < -10)] = 1\\\\n    bins[(distance >= -10) & (distance < 0)] = 2\\\\n    bins[distance == 0] = 3\\\\n    bins[(distance > 0) & (distance <= 10)] = 4\\\\n    bins[(distance > 10) & (distance <= 50)] = 5\\\\n    bins[distance > 50] = 6\\\\n    return bins\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef discretize_position(position, n_bins=5):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Discretize absolute position into n_bins equal-sized bins.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    bin_edges = np.linspace(0, TRACK_LENGTH, n_bins + 1)\\\\n    bins = np.digitize(position, bin_edges[1:])  # 0 to n_bins-1\\\\n    bins = np.clip(bins, 0, n_bins - 1)\\\\n    return bins\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef discretize_speed(speed):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Discretize speed into 5 bins.\\\\n    0: < 2 cm/s\\\\n    1: 2-10 cm/s\\\\n    2: 10-20 cm/s\\\\n    3: 20-40 cm/s\\\\n    4: > 40 cm/s\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    bins = np.zeros(len(speed), dtype=np.int64)\\\\n    bins[speed < 2] = 0\\\\n    bins[(speed >= 2) & (speed < 10)] = 1\\\\n    bins[(speed >= 10) & (speed < 20)] = 2\\\\n    bins[(speed >= 20) & (speed < 40)] = 3\\\\n    bins[speed >= 40] = 4\\\\n    return bins\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef process_licks(lick_data, trial_start_inds, teleport_inds):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Process lick data following reference code logic.\\\\n    1. Detect and remove lick sensor errors\\\\n    2. Clip to [0, 1] (binary)\\\\n    3. Smooth with Gaussian\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    licks = np.copy(lick_data).astype(np.float64)\\\\n    \\\\n    # Lick sensor error correction per trial\\\\n    for t in range(len(trial_start_inds)):\\\\n        t_start = trial_start_inds[t]\\\\n        t_end = teleport_inds[t]\\\\n        trial_licks = licks[t_start:t_end]\\\\n        \\\\n        # If >35% of samples have cumulative lick count > 2, set to NaN\\\\n        if len(trial_licks) > 0:\\\\n            frac_high = np.sum(trial_licks > 2) / len(trial_licks)\\\\n            if frac_high > LICK_ERROR_THRESHOLD:\\\\n                licks[t_start:t_end] = np.nan\\\\n    \\\\n    # Clip to [0, 1]\\\\n    licks[licks > 1] = 1\\\\n    \\\\n    return licks\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef process_session(nwb_path, show_processing=False, session_idx=0):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Process a single NWB file and return trial-level data.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    t0 = time.time()\\\\n    \\\\n    f = h5py.File(nwb_path, 'r')\\\\n    \\\\n    # Extract metadata\\\\n    subj_id = f['general']['subject']['subject_id'][()].decode()\\\\n    sess_id = f['general']['session_id'][()].decode()\\\\n    \\\\n    # Extract behavioral data\\\\n    beh = f['processing']['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries']\\\\n    position = beh['position']['data'][:]\\\\n    speed_data = beh['speed']['data'][:]\\\\n    lick_data = beh['lick']['data'][:]\\\\n    rzone = beh['reward_zone']['data'][:]\\\\n    env_data = beh['environment']['data'][:]\\\\n    trial_start_markers = beh['trial_start']['data'][:]\\\\n    teleport_markers = beh['teleport']['data'][:]\\\\n    scanning = beh['scanning']['data'][:]\\\\n    reward_timestamps = beh['Reward']['timestamps'][:]\\\\n    pos_timestamps = beh['position']['timestamps'][:]\\\\n    \\\\n    # Extract neural data\\\\n    deconv_data = f['processing']['ophys']['Deconvolved']['plane0']['data'][:]  # (n_timepoints, n_rois)\\\\n    iscell = f['processing']['ophys']['ImageSegmentation']['PlaneSegmentation']['iscell'][:]\\\\n    \\\\n    f.close()\\\\n    \\\\n    # Filter neurons by iscell\\\\n    cell_mask = iscell[:, 0] == 1\\\\n    neural_all = deconv_data[:, cell_mask].T  # (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\\\\n    n_neurons = neural_all.shape[0]\\\\n    n_timepoints = neural_all.shape[1]\\\\n    \\\\n    # Get trial boundaries\\\\n    trial_start_inds = np.where(trial_start_markers > 0)[0]\\\\n    teleport_inds = np.where(teleport_markers > 0)[0]\\\\n    n_trials = len(trial_start_inds)\\\\n    \\\\n    if n_trials != len(teleport_inds):\\\\n        print(f\\\\\\\"  WARNING: trial_start ({n_trials}) != teleport ({len(teleport_inds)}) count\\\\\\\")\\\\n        n_trials = min(n_trials, len(teleport_inds))\\\\n        trial_start_inds = trial_start_inds[:n_trials]\\\\n        teleport_inds = teleport_inds[:n_trials]\\\\n    \\\\n    # Compute frame rate\\\\n    dt = np.median(np.diff(pos_timestamps))\\\\n    \\\\n    # Get reward zone info per trial\\\\n    rz_starts, rz_labels = get_reward_zone_start_per_trial(\\\\n        position, rzone, trial_start_inds, teleport_inds)\\\\n    \\\\n    # Process licks\\\\n    licks_processed = process_licks(lick_data, trial_start_inds, teleport_inds)\\\\n    \\\\n    # Determine reward per trial\\\\n    # Convert reward timestamps to frame indices\\\\n    reward_frame_inds = np.searchsorted(pos_timestamps, reward_timestamps)\\\\n    reward_frame_inds = np.clip(reward_frame_inds, 0, n_timepoints - 1)\\\\n    \\\\n    # Build per-trial reward binary\\\\n    trial_rewarded = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=np.int64)\\\\n    for t in range(n_trials):\\\\n        t_start = trial_start_inds[t]\\\\n        t_end = teleport_inds[t]\\\\n        # Check if any reward was delivered in this trial\\\\n        reward_in_trial = np.any(\\\\n            (reward_frame_inds >= t_start) & (reward_frame_inds < t_end)\\\\n        )\\\\n        trial_rewarded[t] = 1 if reward_in_trial else 0\\\\n    \\\\n    # Get environment type per trial\\\\n    trial_env = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=np.int64)\\\\n    for t in range(n_trials):\\\\n        t_start = trial_start_inds[t]\\\\n        t_end = teleport_inds[t]\\\\n        env_vals = env_data[t_start:t_end]\\\\n        env_vals = env_vals[env_vals >= 0]  # exclude -1\\\\n        if len(env_vals) > 0:\\\\n            trial_env[t] = int(np.median(env_vals))\\\\n    \\\\n    # Get reward zone label per trial (for output)\\\\n    trial_rz_label = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=np.int64)\\\\n    rz_label_map = {'A': 0, 'B': 1, 'C': 2}\\\\n    for t in range(n_trials):\\\\n        label = get_reward_zone_for_trial(rz_labels, t)\\\\n        trial_rz_label[t] = rz_label_map.get(label, 0)\\\\n    \\\\n    # Get reward zone start position per trial (for distance computation)\\\\n    # For omission trials, use the same reward zone as neighboring trials\\\\n    trial_rz_start = np.zeros(n_trials)\\\\n    for t in range(n_trials):\\\\n        label = get_reward_zone_for_trial(rz_labels, t)\\\\n        trial_rz_start[t] = REWARD_ZONES[label][0]\\\\n    \\\\n    # Build trial data\\\\n    neural_trials = []\\\\n    input_trials = []\\\\n    output_trials = []\\\\n    \\\\n    for t in range(n_trials):\\\\n        t_start = trial_start_inds[t]\\\\n        t_end = teleport_inds[t]\\\\n        n_tp = t_end - t_start\\\\n        \\\\n        if n_tp < 2:\\\\n            continue\\\\n        \\\\n        # Neural data for this trial\\\\n        trial_neural = neural_all[:, t_start:t_end].astype(np.float32)\\\\n        \\\\n        # --- INPUTS ---\\\\n        # Time from start of trial (seconds)\\\\n        time_from_start = np.arange(n_tp) * dt\\\\n        \\\\n        # Environment type (binary, per trial)\\\\n        env_type = float(trial_env[t])\\\\n        \\\\n        # Trial number (continuous, per trial)\\\\n        trial_num = float(t)\\\\n        \\\\n        # Previous trial outcome (binary, per trial)\\\\n        if t == 0:\\\\n            prev_outcome = 0.0\\\\n        else:\\\\n            prev_outcome = float(trial_rewarded[t - 1])\\\\n        \\\\n        # Build input array\\\\n        # Time-varying: time_from_start (n_tp,)\\\\n        # Per-trial: env_type, trial_num, prev_outcome\\\\n        input_data = np.zeros((4, n_tp), dtype=np.float32)\\\\n        input_data[0, :] = time_from_start\\\\n        input_data[1, :] = env_type\\\\n        input_data[2, :] = trial_num\\\\n        input_data[3, :] = prev_outcome\\\\n        \\\\n        # --- OUTPUTS ---\\\\n        trial_pos = position[t_start:t_end]\\\\n        trial_speed = speed_data[t_start:t_end]\\\\n        trial_licks = licks_processed[t_start:t_end]\\\\n        \\\\n        # Distance to reward zone (time-varying, discretized)\\\\n        rz_start = trial_rz_start[t]\\\\n        distance = compute_distance_to_reward_zone(trial_pos, rz_start)\\\\n        dist_bins = discretize_distance(distance)\\\\n        \\\\n        # Absolute position (time-varying, discretized into 5 bins)\\\\n        pos_bins = discretize_position(trial_pos, n_bins=5)\\\\n        \\\\n        # Speed (time-varying, discretized)\\\\n        speed_bins = discretize_speed(np.abs(trial_speed))  # use absolute speed\\\\n        \\\\n        # Lick (time-varying, binary)\\\\n        lick_binary = np.zeros(n_tp, dtype=np.int64)\\\\n        if not np.all(np.isnan(trial_licks)):\\\\n            # Smooth licks\\\\n            smoothed_licks = nansmooth(trial_licks, LICK_SMOOTH_SIGMA)\\\\n            # Convert to binary: > 0.5 threshold after smoothing\\\\n            lick_binary = (smoothed_licks > 0.5).astype(np.int64)\\\\n            lick_binary[np.isnan(smoothed_licks)] = 0\\\\n        \\\\n        # Reward zone location (per-trial)\\\\n        rz_loc = trial_rz_label[t]\\\\n        \\\\n        # Reward outcome (per-trial)\\\\n        reward_out = trial_rewarded[t]\\\\n        \\\\n        # Build output array\\\\n        # Time-varying: dist_bins, pos_bins, speed_bins, lick_binary\\\\n        # Per-trial: rz_loc, reward_out\\\\n        output_data = np.zeros((6, n_tp), dtype=np.int64)\\\\n        output_data[0, :] = dist_bins\\\\n        output_data[1, :] = pos_bins\\\\n        output_data[2, :] = speed_bins\\\\n        output_data[3, :] = lick_binary\\\\n        output_data[4, :] = rz_loc\\\\n        output_data[5, :] = reward_out\\\\n        \\\\n        neural_trials.append(trial_neural)\\\\n        input_trials.append(input_data)\\\\n        output_trials.append(output_data)\\\\n    \\\\n    elapsed = time.time() - t0\\\\n    print(f\\\\\\\"  {subj_id} ses-{sess_id}: {n_neurons} neurons, {len(neural_trials)} trials, \\\\\\\"\\\\n          f\\\\\\\"{n_tp} timepoints (last trial), dt={dt*1000:.1f}ms, {elapsed:.1f}s\\\\\\\")\\\\n    \\\\n    if show_processing and session_idx < 2:\\\\n        plot_processing(subj_id, sess_id, position, speed_data, licks_processed,\\\\n                       trial_start_inds, teleport_inds, neural_all, \\\\n                       rz_starts, rz_labels, trial_rewarded, trial_env,\\\\n                       pos_timestamps, dt, neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials,\\\\n                       session_idx)\\\\n    \\\\n    return {\\\\n        'neural_trials': neural_trials,\\\\n        'input_trials': input_trials,\\\\n        'output_trials': output_trials,\\\\n        'subj_id': subj_id,\\\\n        'sess_id': sess_id,\\\\n        'n_neurons': n_neurons,\\\\n        'dt': dt,\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef plot_processing(subj_id, sess_id, position, speed, licks,\\\\n                   trial_start_inds, teleport_inds, neural_all,\\\\n                   rz_starts, rz_labels, trial_rewarded, trial_env,\\\\n                   pos_timestamps, dt, neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials,\\\\n                   session_idx):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Plot processing steps for visual verification.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    import matplotlib\\\\n    matplotlib.use('Agg')\\\\n    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\\\\n    \\\\n    fig, axes = plt.subplots(6, 2, figsize=(20, 24))\\\\n    fig.suptitle(f'{subj_id} ses-{sess_id}', fontsize=16)\\\\n    \\\\n    n_trials = len(trial_start_inds)\\\\n    \\\\n    # Plot 1: Position over time for first 10 trials\\\\n    ax = axes[0, 0]\\\\n    for t in range(min(10, n_trials)):\\\\n        t_start = trial_start_inds[t]\\\\n        t_end = teleport_inds[t]\\\\n        ts = pos_timestamps[t_start:t_end] - ax.set_title('Position traces (first 10 trials)')\\\\n    ax.legend(fontsize=6)\\\\n    \\\\n    # Plot 2: Speed distribution\\\\n    ax = axes[0, 1]\\\\n    valid_speed = speed[speed > -100]\\\\n    ax.hist(valid_speed, bins=100, range=(-5, 80))\\\\n    ax.axvline(2, color='r', linestyle='--', label='Speed threshold')\\\\n    ax.set_xlabel('Speed (cm/s)')\\\\n    ax.set_title('Speed      ax.set_title('Distance to RZ (Trial 0)')\\\\n    \\\\n    # Plot 6: Position bins (first trial)\\\\n    ax = axes[2, 1]\\\\n    if len(output_trials) > 0:\\\\n        ax.plot(output_trials[0][1, main():\\\\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Convert NWB data to decoder format')\\\\n    parser.add_argument('output', help='Output pickle file path')\\\\n    parser.add_argument('--full', action='store_true', default=True, help='Process all sessions')\\\\n    parser.add_argument('--sample', action='store_true', help='Process only 2 sessions')\\\\n    parser.add_argument('--show-processing', action='store_true', help='Show processing plots')\\\\n    args = parser.parse_args()\\\\n    \\\\n    if args.sample:\\\\n        args.full = False\\\\n    \\\\n    print(\\\\\\\"=\\\\\\\" * 60)\\\\n    print(\\\\\\\"NWB to Decoder Format Conversion\\\\\\\")\\\\n    print(\\\\\\\"=\\\\\\\" * 60)\\\\n    \\\\n    # Find all NWB files\\\\n    nwb_files = sorted(glob.glob('data/sub-*/sub-*_ses-*_behavior+ophys.nwb'))\\\\n    print(f\\\\\\\"Found {len(nwb_files)} NWB files\\\\\\\")\\\\n    \\\\n    if args.sample:\\\\n        # Select 2 sessions from \\\\n    # Process all sessions\\\\n    all_neural = []\\\\n    all_input = []\\\\n    all_output = []\\\\n    all_subj_ids = []\\\\n    all_sess_ids = []\\\\n    all_n_neurons = []\\\\n    all_dts = If the GPU does not have sufficient RAM for the network training, use the flag `--cpu` to specify to use the CPU to train. \\n2. **Wait for complete execution** \\u2014 this may take significant time for large datasets\\n3. **Check training**: Verify loss decreases over epochs\\n4. **Check accuracy**: High accuracy is an indicator that data conversion has been done correctly. Accuracy near chance is a sign that there might be issues in temporal alignment of signals, choice of data streams, or filtering or processing of data. Compare accuracy to expectations based on the paper. \\n\\n**Done when**: \\n1. Full decoder training completes (the script finishes running)\\n2. Accuracy results are documented in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 11\\\" with a table of accuracies\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 12: Critical Review 2\\n\\n**Goal**: Find and fix any errors by performing the following checks. Fix issues and re-run affected steps. Iterate until no issues remain. Perform all of the following checks:\\n\\n**Check 1: Accuracy vs chance analysis**\\n- For each output, compare validation accuracy to chance (1/num_classes)\\n- Accuracy below chance indicates a bug, investigate and fix conversion issues to improve this. \\n- Accuracy below 1.5x chance may also indicate a bug, investigate whether changes in conversion logic could improve accuracy. \\n\\n**Check 2: Accuracy comparison to paper**\\n- Find every decoding accuracy reported in the reference paper\\n- Create a table comparing your accuracy to the paper's accuracy for each variable\\n- If your accuracy is lower than the reported accuracy, this may indicate a bug in your conversion that you must fix. \\n- Differences in algorithm/architecture should be relatively small because of the data dimensionality and size. Do not use this as an excuse to dismiss differences, investigate them completely before moving on. \\n\\n**Check 3: Train vs validation gap**\\n- If training accuracy is much higher (>1.5x) than validation accuracy for any output, investigate overfitting or data leakage. \\n\\n**If accuracy is low for an output, try these specific debugging steps:**\\n1. Verify the output values are correct by loading raw data and checking 3 specific trials\\n2. Check temporal alignment \\u2014 plot neural + output for a single trial to verify they're synchronized\\n3. Check whether the output has enough variation (not 99% one class)\\n4. Check that filtering steps for neural activity streams are followed. \\n5. Check that processing of the data matches the reference code and paper. \\n\\n**Iteration protocol**: If ANY check above reveals an issue:\\n1. Fix the issue in convert_data.py\\n2. Re-run the affected conversion and validation steps\\n3. Re-run ALL checks in this step (not just the one that failed)\\n4. Document each iteration: what was found, what was fixed, what the re-check showed\\n\\n**Report all checks and results** to `CONVERSION_NOTES.md` to convince the user that the conversion and decoding has been done correctly. \\n\\n**Done when**: You have documented your review findings and all issues are resolved in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 12\\\".\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 13: Documentation and Cleanup\\n\\n**Goal**: Finalize documentation and organize files.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Ensure CONVERSION_NOTES.md is complete with all:\\n  - Key decisions and rationale\\n  - Checks for correctness of the conversion\\n  - Validation results and tables\\n  - Any issues found and how they were resolved\\n- Create a user-facing `README.md` summarizing:\\n  - Dataset description\\n  - How to load and use the converted data\\n  - Output format specification\\n  - Key statistics\\n- Move analysis/investigation scripts to a `cache/` folder\\n- Create `cache/README_CACHE.md` documenting cached files\\n\\n**Done when**: README.md exists, CONVERSION_NOTES.md is complete, and directory is clean.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## CONVERSION_NOTES.md Template\\n\\n**Create this file IMMEDIATELY in Step 0. 71 interior bytes omitted ...]\\ne a cumulative lick count in each frame, so in my behavior code anything >1 gets set to 1 to be able to convert it accurately to a rate when I w\\r\\nant to convert it to Hz per position bin or time bin\\r\\n    * 'rewards' is just a binary at the sample where reward was delivered\\r\\n    * 'speed' is an actual smoothed running speed in cm/s for each sample.\\r\\n* `trial_matrices` are the spatially binned versions of timeseries, in bins of 10 cm, from 0 to 450 cm (not including the teleport zone). Shape: trials x positi\\r\\non bins x cells.\\r\\n* `trial_start_inds` is a 1 x N trials array of the sample index for the start of each trial (i.e. the start of the track)\\r\\n* `teleport_indices` is a 1 x N trials array of the sample index for the start of the teleport period (i.e. the end of the track)\\r\\n* `vr_data` is a Pandas dataframe of VR behavior data converted from the sqlite files output by Unity and already synchronized with the imaging data\\r\\n\\r\\nThe sess class, which aligns the VR data to the imaging data, is generated by [preprocessing.vr_align_to_2P](https://github.com/GiocomoLab/TwoPUtils/blob/00b658\\r\\n9e5afea4cfe2347557b0a2450d9673c435/TwoPUtils/preprocessing.py#L124) in the [TwoPUtils](https://github.com/GiocomoLab/TwoPUtils/tree/main) repo. Please review th\\r\\nis function carefully to understand how the VR data are pre-processed and written into sess.vr_data.\\r\\n\\r\\nIn multi_anim_sess['GCAMP4']['sess'].vr_data, there is one row per position in cm on a virtual linear track\\r\\n* `trialnum`: trial number, where each trial is a lap of the track\\r\\n* `dz`: delta in position from one sample to the next\\r\\n* `speed`: the speed of the mouse in cm/s\\r\\n* `lick`: lick detection by capacitive sensor; preprocessed cumulatively per imaging frame\\r\\n* `reward`: a binary of when reward was delivered\\r\\n* `rzone`: a binary flag Discretized into bins:\\n  - 0: < 2 cm/s\\n  - 1: 2-10 cm/s\\n  - 2: 10-20 cm/s\\n  - 3: 20-40 cm/s\\n  - 4: > 40 cm/s\\n- Lick, time-varying. 0 = no, 1 = yes\\n- Reward zone location, per-trial. 0 = A, 1 = B, 2 = C\\n- Reward outcome, per-trial. 0 = no, 1 = yes\\n\\n## Target Data Format\\n\\n- Save the full converted dataset to the pickle file `converted_data.pkl`.\\n- All datasets must be converted into the following Python dictionary structure:\\n\\n```python\\ndata = {\\n    'neural': [  # list of sessions\\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # trial 2\\n            ...\\n        ],\\n        [  # list of trials for session 2\\n            ...\\n        ],\\n        ...\\n    ],\\n\\n    'input': [  # list of sessions\\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\\n            input_data,  # stimulus/task variables, shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input)\\n            ...\\n        ],\\n        ...\\n    ],\\n\\n    'output': [  # list of sessions\\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\\n            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)\\n            ...\\n        ],\\n        ...\\n    ],\\n\\n    'subjects': list of str, # ids of all subjects, length n_subjects\\n    'subject_idx': shape (n_sessions,), # index into subjects for each session\\n\\n    'brain_regions': list of str, # names of the brain regions recorded from, e.g. ALM, V1\\n    'brain_region_idx': [ # list of sessions\\n        neuron_region_idx, # shape: (n_neurons,)\\n    ], # index into `brain_regions` for each neuron\\n\\n    'input_names': list of str, # names for each input, of length n_input\\n    'output_names': list of str, # names of each output, of length n_output\\n    'output_values': [ # list of length n_output\\n        [ output_val0, ... ], # list of str of length d_output[0], name of each output value\\n        ...\\n    ],\\n\\n    'metadata': {\\n        'task_description': str, # description of output tasks\\n        'time_bin_size': float, # length of time bin in ms\\n        'temporal_alignment_event': str, # description of alignment event\\n        'off_start': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to start of trial in seconds, None if N/A\\n        'off_end': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to end of trial in seconds, None if N/A\\n        ...\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Key Format Requirements\\n\\n- **neural**: Neural activity data (e.g., firing rates, spike counts) organized by session and trial\\n  - Dimensions: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) for each trial.\\n  - Time bins should be the same size for all trials and sessions. \\n  - There needs to be at least two trials within each session in order to evaluate the decoder performance.\\n\\n- **input**: Variables that serve as inputs **to the decoder**\\n  - These are **decoder inputs**. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \\n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \\n\\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \\n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \\n\\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\\n\\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\\n\\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \\n\\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\\n\\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \\n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \\n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\\n\\n## Python environment\\n\\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\\n\\n## Decoder Reference\\n\\n- Run this script with `python train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\\n- Optional arguments:\\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\\n\\n### Purpose\\n\\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\\n1. Data structure is correct - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \\n2. Dimensions are consistent - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \\n3. Values are sensible - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \\n4. Decoder can successfully train and predict\\n5. Poor performance indicates data formatting issues that need investigation\\n\\n### Consistency requirements\\n\\nYour processing and formatting must **match the reference paper and code** with respect to:\\n- Loading of data\\n- Temporal alignment of different time series streams (neural, inputs, outputs)\\n- Processing of neural, input, and output data streams\\n- Curation of data: filtering of low-quality neurons, trials, sessions, and mice.\\n\\nTo check consistency, you must compare statistics available in the reference paper and your converted dataset. \\n\\nWhenever possible, invent **SANITY CHECKS** that your loading and processing matches the reference paper and code. \\n\\nDiscrepancies are only allowed if required by the Decoder Input and Decoder Output specifications above. \\n\\nCarefully verify your work after every step. When you find mistakes, document and fix them immediately. Be critical of results **after every step of processing**. \\n\\nYou will be assessed on whether the decisions you make on how to load, filter, process, align, reformat, and save the data are reasonable and match the reference paper and code and these instructions. During testing, the reference version of `train_decoder.py` will be run on your converted data. Data statistics and decoder accuracy will be compared to those achieved by human-written conversion code. \\n\\n---\\n\\n## Conversion Workflow\\n\\n**IMPORTANT**: Follow these steps in order. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\\n   301→\\n   302→i. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. The reward zone boundaries come from the `reward_zone` behavior time series. This variable is non-zero when the mouse is in the reward zone. I combine this with the position of the mouse when this is non-zero to figure out the closest reward zone. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \\n   303→\\n   304→ii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \\n   305→- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. It first computes the position of the min and max position of the mouse when `reward_zone` is non-zero:\\n   306→```python\\n   307→behavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \\n   308→info['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\\n   309→position = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\\n   310→for trial in range(ntrials):\\n   311→    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\\n   312→    pos_trial = position[idx]\\n   313→    reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\\n   314→    if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\\n   315→        continue\\n   316→    info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\\n   317→```\\n   318→The function `segment_reward_positions()` uses the Viterbi algorithm to assign reward zone labels so that the initial rewarded positions are close to the corresponding rewarded zone:\\n   319→```python\\n   320→reward_zone_dict = {'A': [80, 130],\\n   321→                    'B': [200, 250],\\n   322→                    'C': [320, 370]}\\n   323→...\\n   324→sigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\\n   325→zone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\\n   326→dist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\\n   327→                    startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\\n   328→dist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\\n   329→log_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\\n   330→```\\n   331→It also encourages the reward zone label to not change often:\\n   332→```python\\n   333→pstay = .9\\n   334→log_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\\n   335→np.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\\n   336→```\\n   337→\\n   338→iii. The paper defines reward zones A, B, C at specific position ranges. These same ranges could also be found, with some translation, in the code (required mapping X -> A, etc.). I plotted the position of the mouse when `reward_zone` was positive (note that the value was between 0 and 6 I think) to determine that the Viterbi approach would likely work, and that the start of the rewarded position was the least noisy variable to use. The class fractions were approximately 1/3 after this, so it seemed correct. \\n   339→\\n   340→## 7-b. The value is constant across all timepoints within a trial.\\n\\nii.\\n```python\\nif trial == 0:\\n    input_curr[3,:] = 0\\nelse:\\n    prev_reward_idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial-1], trial_end_idx[trial-1], dtype=int)\\n    isprevreward = np.any(isreward[prev_reward_idx])\\n    input_curr[3,:] = int(isprevreward)\\n```\\n\\niii. The instructions specify previous trial outcome as binary (omitted=0, rewarded=1). The code checks if any reward event fell within the previous trial's time boundaries.\\n\\n## 7-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\\n\\ni. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. The reward zone boundaries come from the `reward_zone` behavior time series. This variable is non-zero when the mouse is in the reward zone. I combine this with the position of the mouse when this is non-zero to figure out the closest reward zone. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \\n\\nii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \\n- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. It first computes the position of the min and max position of the mouse when `reward_zone` is non-zero:\\n```python\\nbehavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \\ninfo['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\\nposition = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\\nfor trial in range(ntrials):\\n    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\\n    pos_trial = position[idx]\\n    reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\\n    if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\\n        continue\\n    info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\\n```\\nThe function `segment_reward_positions()` uses the Viterbi algorithm to assign reward zone labels so that the initial rewarded positions are close to the corresponding rewarded zone:\\n```python\\nreward_zone_dict = {'A': [80, 130],\\n                    'B': [200, 250],\\n                    'C': [320, 370]}\\n...\\nsigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\\nzone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\\ndist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\\n                    startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\\ndist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\\nlog_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\\n```\\nIt also encourages the reward zone label to not change often:\\n```python\\npstay = .9\\nlog_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\\nnp.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\\n```\\n\\niii. The paper defines reward zones A, B, C at specific position ranges. These same ranges could also be found, with some translation, in the code (required mapping X -> A, etc.). I plotted the position of the mouse when `reward_zone` was positive (note that the value was between 0 and 6 I think) to determine that the Viterbi approach would likely work, and that the start of the rewarded position was the least noisy variable to use. The class fractions were approximately 1/3 after this, so it seemed correct. \\n\\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\\n\\ni. For each timepoint, compute the signed distance from the animal's position to the nearest edge of the reward zone. Distance is 0 when inside the zone, negative when before the zone, and positive when past it.\\n\\nii.\\n```python\\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr):\\n    ntimepoints = len(position_curr)\\n    reward_zone_range = reward_zone_dict[reward_zone_curr]\\n    distance_to_reward_zone = np.zeros(ntimepoints)\\n    idx_before_zone = position_curr < reward_zone_range[0]\\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_before_zone] = position_curr[idx_before_zone] - reward_zone_range[0]\\n    idx_after_zone = position_curr > reward_zone_range[1]\\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_after_zone] = position_curr[idx_after_zone] - reward_zone_range[1]\\n    return distance_to_reward_zone\\n```\\n\\niii. This matches the paper's concept of distance relative to the reward zone. The reward zone boundaries are from `reward_zone_dict`, inspired by the reference code `Sosa_et_al_2024/src/reward_relative/behavior.py`.\\n\\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* thresholded into categories?\\n\\ni. The continuous distance is discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\\n\\nii.\\n```python\\ndistance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\\n...\\noutput_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\\n```\\n\\niii. The bin edges match the instructions. The `1e-6` boundary separates exactly 0 (in the zone boundary) from slightly positive. The `-1` corrects `np.digitize` to be 0-indexed.\\n\\n## 7-d. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* aligned with the neural data?\\n\\ni. The position data and neural data share the same time indices within each trial, so no additional alignment is needed.\\n\\nii.\\n```python\\nidx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\\nspike_data_curr = spike_data[idx]\\nposition_curr = position[idx]\\n```\\n\\niii. Both neural and behavioral data use the same time indexing (verified by timestamp assertions earlier in the code), so indexing by the same `idx` array ensures alignment.\\n\\n## 8-a. No processing beyond extracting the per-trial slice and discretizing.\\n\\nii.\\n```python\\nposition_curr = position[idx]\\noutput_curr[1] = np.digitize(position_curr, position_bins) - 1\\n```\\n\\niii. The raw position values are used directly.\\n\\n## 8-c. How is `output` *Absolute position* thresholded into categories?\\n\\ni. Discretized into 5 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, 50, 150, 250, 350, inf]`, corresponding to 100 cm wide bins spanning the corridor. Same indexing as neural: `position_curr = position[idx]`\\n\\niii. Verified by timestamp assertions.\\n\\n## 9-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Lick* derived from?\\n\\ni. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\\n\\ni. Several cases are handled:\\n- **Neural/behavior length mismatch**: If the number of neural time bins differs from behavior timestamps, data is cropped to the minimum of the two with a warning printed.\\n- **Short trials**: Trials with fewer than 50 timepoints (`min_ntimepoints`) are skipped with a warning.\\n- **Missing reward zone data**: Trials where `reward_zone` is never active (all zeros) get NaN positions, and the Viterbi algorithm handles these via uniform emission (assignment driven by neighboring trials' transitions).\\n- **Reward timestamp alignment**: An assertion verifies reward times align within half a time bin of behavior timestamps.\\n\\nii.\\n```python\\nif T != len(timestamps):\\n    print(f\\\"Warning: number of neural time bins ({T}) does not match number of behavior timestamps ({len(timestamps)}), cropping to the minimum of the two\\\")\\n    T = min(T, len(timestamps))\\n    spike_data = spike_data[:T]\\n    timestamps = timestamps[:T]\\n...\\nif idx.sum() < min_ntimepoints:\\n    print(f\\\"Skipping trial {trial}...\\\")\\n    istrial[trial] = False\\n    continue\\n```\\n\\niii. These are defensive checks found during data exploration. The neural/behavior mismatch occurs in a small number of sessions.\\n\\n## 13-a. What are the most time-consuming steps of the code?\\n\\ni. The most time-consuming steps are:\\n1. **Loading NWB files** (`pynwb.NWBHDF5IO` and reading large arrays) — I/O bound\\n2. **The survey step** — loads every NWB file to gather statistics and reward zone positions\\n3. **Full conversion** — loads every NWB file again and extracts all trial data\\n4. **Saving the .pkl file**\\n\\nii. N/A\\n\\niii. The NWB files are large (contain full neural recordings). Conversion is otherwise quite fast\\n\\n## 13-b. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\\n\\ni. The per-trial loop in `convert_session_data` (lines 267-332) iterates over each trial sequentially. Some operations like `np.digitize` and `compute_distance_to_reward_zone` could theoretically be applied to the full session arrays before splitting into trials, but the variable trial lengths make this awkward. The Viterbi inner loop (lines 503-507) iterates over states, which could be vectorized with matrix operations.\\n\\nii. N/A\\n\\niii. The per-trial loop is the natural structure given variable-length trials. Vectorizing would require padding or masking.\\n\\n## 13-c. What processing does the code repeat multiple times?\\n\\ni. The survey step and the conversion step both load every NWB file and read the same data arrays (neural, behavior). The survey reads neural data to count neurons and check rates, then the conversion reads it again. The `reward_zone_positions` are computed in the survey and then used in the conversion, but other data (position, speed, lick, etc.) is read twice. \\n\\nii. N/A\\n\\niii. I don't think these could be run at the same time, as it would require too much RAM. The Viterbi output created during surveying is required to process the data. It was convenient to run the survey before deciding how to handle the conversion of the data. \\n\\n## 13-d.  399→    all_info = {}\\n   400→    subjects = get_subjects(datadir=datadir)\\n   401→    all_info['reward_zone_positions'] = {}\\n   402→    fig,ax = plt.subplots(1,len(subjects),   464→    with open(surveyfile, 'wb') as f:\\n   465→        pickle.dump(all_info, f)\\n   466→        \\n   467→    return all_info\\n   468→\\n   469→def segment_reward_positions(reward_zone_positions):\\n   470→    # assign each trial to one of the reward zones defined in reward_zone_dict\\n   471→    # use viterbi algorithm with a high cost for switching to encourage stable assignments\\n   472→    zone_names = sorted(reward_zone_dict.keys())\\n   473→    n_states = len(zone_names)\\n   474→    zone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\\n   475→    pstay = .9\\n   476→    sigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\\n   477→\\n   478→    # transition log-probabilities\\n   479→    log_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\\n   480→    np.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\\n   481→\\n   482→    results = {}\\n   483→\\n   484→    for mouse_id, positions in reward_zone_positions.items():\\n   485→        n_trials = positions.shape[0]\\n   486→        startpoints = positions[:,0] # use the start point as it looks cleaner\\n   487→        valid = ~np.isnan(startpoints)\\n   488→\\n   489→        # emission log-probabilities: Gaussian penalty based on distance to zone range\\n   490→        # distance is 0 if inside [lo, hi], otherwise distance to nearest edge\\n   491→        # for NaN trials, uniform emission (all zeros) so assignment is driven by transitions\\n   492→        log_emission = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states))\\n   493→        dist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\\n   494→                          startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\\n   495→        dist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\\n   496→        log_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\\n   497→\\n   498→        # viterbi forward pass\\n   499→        log_delta = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states))\\n   500→        psi = np.zeros((n_trials, n_states), dtype=int)\\n   501→        log_delta[0] = log_emission[0]  # uniform prior\\n   502→        for t in range(1, n_trials):\\n   503→            for k in range(n_states):\\n   504→                scores = log_delta[t - 1] + log_trans[:, k]\\n   505→                psi[t, k] = np.argmax(scores)\\n   506→                log_delta[t, k] = scores[psi[t, k]] + log_emission[t, k]\\n   507→\\n   508→        # backtrack\\n   509→        states = np.zeros(n_trials, dtype=int)\\n   510→        states[-1] = np.argmax(log_delta[-1])\\n   511→        for t in range(n_trials - 2, -1, -1):\\n   512→            states[t] = psi[t + 1, states[t + 1]]\\n   513→\\n   514→        # convert state indices to zone names\\n   515→        zone_labels = np.array([zone_names[s] for s in states])\\n   516→\\n   517→        # distance from each trial's startpoint to its assigned zone range\\n   518→        assigned_lo = zone_ranges[states, 0]\\n   519→        assigned_hi = zone_ranges[states, 1]\\n   520→        zone_dist = np.maximum(np.maximum(assigned_lo - startpoints, startpoints - assigned_hi), 0)\\n   521→        zone_dist[~valid] = np.nan\\n   522→\\n   523→        results[mouse_id] = {'zone_labels': zone_labels, 'states': states, 'zone_dist': zone_dist}\\n   524→\\n   525→    return results\\n   526→    \\n   527→\\n   528→def main():\\n   529→\\n   530→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Convert Sosa et al. 2024 NWB data to pickle format.')\\n   531→ The reward zone boundaries come from the `reward_zone` behavior time series. This variable is non-zero when the mouse is in the reward zone. I combine this with the position of the mouse when this is non-zero to figure out the closest reward zone. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \\n\\nii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \\n- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. It first computes the position of the min and max position of the mouse when `reward_zone` is non-zero:\\n```python\\nbehavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \\ninfo['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\\nposition = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\\nfor trial in range(ntrials):\\n    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\\n    pos_trial = position[idx]\\n    reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\\n    if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\\n        continue\\n    info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\\n```\\nThe function `segment_reward_positions()` uses the Viterbi algorithm to assign reward zone labels so that the initial rewarded positions are close to the corresponding rewarded zone:\\n```python\\nreward_zone_dict = {'A': [80, 130],\\n                    'B': [200, 250],\\n                    'C': [320, 370]}\\n...\\nsigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\\nzone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\\ndist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\\n                    startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\\ndist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\\nlog_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\\n```\\nIt also encourages the reward zone label to not change often:\\n```python\\npstay = .9\\nlog_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\\nnp.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\\n```\\n\\niii. The paper defines reward zones A, B, C at specific position ranges. These same ranges could also be found, with some translation, in the code (required mapping X -> A, etc.). I plotted the position of the mouse when `reward_zone` was positive (note that the value was between 0 and 6 I think) to determine that the Viterbi approach would likely work, and that the start of the rewarded position was the least noisy variable to use. The class fractions were approximately 1/3 after this, so it seemed correct. \\n\\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\\n\\ni. For each timepoint, compute the signed distance from the animal's position to the nearest edge of the reward zone. Distance is 0 when inside the zone, negative when before the zone, and positive when past it.\\n\\nii.\\n```python\\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr):\\n    ntimepoints = len(position_curr)\\n    reward_zone_range = reward_zone_dict[reward_zone_curr]\\n    distance_to_reward_zone = np.zeros(ntimepoints)\\n    idx_before_zone = position_curr < reward_zone_range[0]\\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_before_zone] = position_curr[idx_before_zone] - reward_zone_range[0]\\n    idx_after_zone = position_curr > reward_zone_range[1]\\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_after_zone] = position_curr[idx_after_zone] - reward_zone_range[1]\\n    return distance_to_reward_zone\\n```\\n\\niii.
